steps.name: A repair is never counted as a morning
steps.description: POST /entries reads the additive optional today claim, classifies after validate_entry_date through the pure core, records entry_ms as NULL for a backdated save, and stamps backdated true on its entry.saved payload. Response shape unchanged.

A backdated save records entry_ms NULL in the row and on the trail — zero speed samples — and carries backdated true for the repair counter
A same-day save keeps its timing: one speed sample gained, repair counter unmoved; correcting a timed morning leaves the week's samples and median intact

phases.name: Phase 03 — The one hint line, the client contract, and the calm dress (D-24/D8/A22, milestone-10 close)

steps.name: One hint line serves anchor, edit and gap
steps.description: The yesterday-reference node becomes a single entry-hint node, never removed, filled by a pure hintFor over the embedded map with a dayLabel extracted from entryRowText. The submit payload carries the picked date plus the today claim, and after a save the row resets to today.
criteria: GET / carries exactly one hint node, id entry-hint, on every render; id yesterday-reference no longer appears anywhere on the page
Pure hintFor answers three mutually exclusive states: the yesterday anchor on today, Editing {day} — was {v} kg, and No entry for {day} yet
The hint names its day through a dayLabel shared with entryRowText — one Fri 24 Jul grammar, never a second calendar wording
Submit sends the picked date and the device-local today claim; after a successful save the row returns to today, the field clears, the hint re-derives
The save response's date, weight_kg and recent merge into the client map, so anchor and prefill stay fresh with no reload
steps.implementation_notes: EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: this step's contract is a single-shot browser UI flow in the one inline script — hint wording, submitted payload and post-save reset are golden-text and event-order pins that no Hypothesis strategy can quantify in a browser-less suite. Compensate with property-based test at unit level on adjacent slot (01-01's bounded_day_frame/is_backdated PBTs and 02-02's record_weights_map projection PBT cover the pure logic the hint and the payload consume). — D-24: ONE #entry-hint node, present on EVERY render and never removed (today's code removes #yesterday-reference, index.html:88) — 'never two hints at once' is structural, not conventional. hintFor(selectedDay, deviceToday, knownWeights) and dayLabel(iso) stay PURE; every DOM write lands at one apply site (FC/IS in the client, ADR-005). dayLabel is extracted from the shipped entryRowText — one Fri 24 Jul grammar, so the hint cannot fork the record's calendar wording; keep 'yesterday: 82.4 kg' verbatim (the AT fallback regex depends on it). OQ-10 wordings are final: 'Editing Thu 23 Jul — was 82.4 kg' / 'No entry for Sun 19 Jul yet'. Submit payload becomes {date: picker value, today: deviceLocalDay(), weight, entry_ms} — this is what makes ADR-011's purity rule falsifiable rather than a client convention. Post-save: dateInput.value = deviceLocalDay(), field cleared, focus back on #weight, hint re-derived; both date/weight_kg and recent are already on the wire, so merging them costs nothing. DELIVER pre-requisite 2: unit-level pins for the submitted payload, the post-save reset and the hint wording land here, plus dogfood verification (client-paint precedent D-15). G-5 must hold: still at most one inline script, zero new external origins. @pending discipline: unskip only this step's 1 scenario.
